T.n: Cash Couriers and Bulk Cash Smuggling

cn.rt: Smuggled or carried cash placed through over-the-counter deposits into personal accounts; physical cash is a branch-only channel.
Sole traders banking inflated cash takings via personal Everyday or savings accounts, mainly over the counter; merchant and business-only elements are out of scope.
Consumers fund gambling and cash out winnings via Everyday account payments and card spend; casino-floor chips and junkets are out of scope.

T.n: Charities and Non-Profit Organisations Misuse for Money Laundering
Freeports, safe deposit boxes and bearer instruments

cn.rt: Funnel accounts take geographically dispersed cash deposits and move funds on fast; retail accounts with branch deposits and digital onward transfer.

T.n: Hawala, Underground Banking and Informal Value Transfer

cn.rt: Personal accounts used as collection points for informal remittance, with cash in at branch and onward digital payments to many parties.

T.n: High-Value Goods (Art, Jewellery, Precious Metals, Luxury Vehicles)

cn.rt: Luxury goods purchases funded by transfers, card spend or loan proceeds; unrelated-party payments and cash handled at branch.
Self-lending and rapid or third-party loan repayment, or term deposit collateral, to give funds a lawful-looking origin.
Core consumer typology: mule accounts receive and forward fraud proceeds via digital channels, with handler-accompanied branch and phone contact.
PEP and associate customer risk can arise across all consumer products, including property lending and lump-sum deposits; a customer-risk typology.
Professional launderers recruit or run multiple personal accounts for third-party flows with fee retention; commercial and trade elements excluded.
Property purchase and mortgage fraud, source of deposit, valuation manipulation and early or third-party payout; funds staged through deposit accounts.

T.n: Sham litigation, arbitration and legal settlements used to launder or justify funds
Sports, sponsorship and club or athlete-transfer laundering

cn.rt: Sub-threshold cash deposits at branch and ATM-linked flows into accounts, term deposit placement, with rapid digital onward movement.
Third-party payments, shared mandates and account use by non-holders across everyday, savings, card repayments and loan funding.

T.n: Trust and Company Service Provider Misuse
Abuse of Non-Profit Organisations and Charities for Terrorist Financing

cn.rt: Charity or community group accounts at a consumer bank receiving collections and forwarding funds offshore; mostly retail-held accounts.

T.n: Crowdfunding and Social Media Fundraising for Terrorist Financing

cn.rt: Donations to crowdfunding or social media appeals paid and received by everyday accounts via remote channels.

T.n: Extortion and Kidnap-for-Ransom Funding of Terrorist Groups

cn.rt: Diaspora or victims send emergency or extortion payments, often cash or third party; coerced payments appear in everyday accounts and in branch, and by phone instruction.

T.n: Foreign Terrorist Fighter Travel and Support Financing

cn.rt: Pre-travel account run-down, cash withdrawals, card use on transit routes and borrowing before departure.

T.n: Hawala and Money or Value Transfer Services for Terrorist Financing

cn.rt: Informal value transfer via cash deposits by many people and pooled receipts into everyday accounts; branch cash and remote transfers.

T.n: Lone Actor and Small-Value Terrorist Funding

cn.rt: Small attacker self-funds from savings, cards and personal loans, with cash-out and purchases; blends into retail banking.

T.n: State Sponsorship and Commodity Trading Funding of Terrorism

cn.rt: Customers send small amounts from everyday accounts to exchanges and self-hosted wallets via remote channels.

T.n: Correspondent Banking and Joint Ventures in Proliferation Financing
DPRK-Style Revenue Generation: Cyber Theft and Overseas IT Workers (Indicator Level)

cn.rt: Mule-style everyday accounts receive remote IT-worker earnings or cyber-theft proceeds, opened and operated digitally.

T.n: Dual-Use Goods Procurement via Front Companies
Maritime Evasion: Flag Hopping, AIS Manipulation and Ship-to-Ship Transfers
Trade Finance and Transshipment Obfuscation for Proliferation

cn.rt: Customers send or receive funds to crypto exchanges and wallets from everyday accounts; custody itself out of scope.

T.n: Luxury Goods and Real-Asset Hiding by Designated Persons

cn.rt: Designated persons buying property via home loans or large transfers; branch and digital funding of purchases; art and yachts out of scope.

T.n: Oil and Commodity Price-Cap and Ship-to-Ship Evasion
Sanctions Evasion via Shell and Ownership Layering (50% Rule Circumvention)

cn.rt: Nominee or relative holds accounts for a designated person; consumer accounts opened digitally or in branch can act as fronts, though corporate layering is out of scope.
Credential, SIM-swap and device takeover enabling payments, card use, fraudulent loan draws, redraw and term deposit break-outs.
Customer-authorised payments from everyday/savings accounts, often under phone coaching; branch tellers can intervene.

T.n: Business Email Compromise and Invoice Redirection

cn.rt: Consumers pay deposits or settlement funds to redirected details on spoofed invoices (e.g. conveyancing, tradespeople); business wire variants are out of scope.
Stolen card details used online or by phone, card testing and chargeback abuse on credit and debit cards.
Counterfeit or returned cheques deposited over the counter or by mobile remote deposit then withdrawn before clearing.

T.n: Cross-border mule and payment-chain laundering of fraud proceeds

cn.rt: Fast onward movement of fraud proceeds through mule everyday and savings accounts into other institutions.

T.n: Elder and Vulnerable Customer Financial Abuse

cn.rt: Third parties, carers or attorneys directing withdrawals, term deposit breaks and borrowing; branch and phone staff are key detection points.
Credit built up then maxed via cash advances and gift cards; personal loan and overdraft first-party default with no intent to repay.
Accounts and credit opened with stolen or synthetic identities across digital, phone and branch origination.
Victims called or texted by impersonators and induced to share codes or move money; card details loaded to wallets.
Victims send savings, including broken term deposits, to scheme operators; operators and mules receive in everyday accounts.
Misstated income, identity or valuation and straw buyers on personal and home loan applications.
Victims pay advance fees and mules receive funds in everyday and savings accounts; cards and in-branch cash also used.

T.n: Payroll, Employee, Insider Fraud and Collusion

cn.rt: Victims send repeated payments to fake partners or platforms, sometimes funded by personal loans; branch staff may spot coercion.

T.n: Scam compounds and end-to-end scam-proceeds flows

cn.rt: Recruited mule everyday and savings accounts collect and consolidate scam proceeds before crypto or offshore cash-out.

T.n: Tax Refund and Identity-Based Benefit Fraud

cn.rt: Fraudulent refunds and benefit payments landing in mule or stolen-identity accounts.
PEP family and associates park proceeds in deposits and buy property with large unexplained deposits; handled mainly face to face or via online banking.
Small cash business owners structure skimmed takings into personal everyday accounts, mainly via branch cash deposits.

T.n: Offshore Tax Evasion and Undeclared Accounts

cn.rt: Undeclared offshore income and assets surface in retail deposits, term deposits and loans with foreign funds and residency inconsistencies.

T.n: Transfer pricing and intra-group profit shifting abuse
Forced Labour in Supply Chains and Employment

cn.rt: Worker accounts and cards controlled by employers or recruiters, wage skimming, recruitment-fee debt and coerced loans.
Third-party controlled accounts, cash deposits, adverts and travel/accommodation spend, plus coerced credit.
Fees paid by migrants or families via cash deposits and transfers to facilitator accounts.
Small recurring payments to individuals or sites by card or fast payment from personal accounts.

T.n: Illegal Mining and Precious Metals Laundering
Account Takeover and Money Mule Account Networks (Cyber Angle)

cn.rt: Takeover and mule accounts moving scam proceeds; loan and card takeover enables cash-out, and call centre used for social engineering and credential resets.
Hard call: kiosk is outside the bank, but scam victims coached by phone withdraw cash or cash-advance to feed kiosks; visible as unusual cash withdrawals and transfers.
Customers fund darknet purchases or cash out proceeds through everyday account payments to exchanges and P2P sellers.

T.n: NFT and Online Gaming / In-Game Currency Laundering
Neobank and Fintech Account Abuse via Rapid Onboarding

cn.rt: Rapid remote onboarding to open mule or pass-through accounts in bulk.

T.n: Online Marketplace and Gig-Economy Platform Misuse
Payment Facilitator, High-Risk Merchant and Transaction Laundering
Prepaid Cards and Stored Value Abuse
Synthetic and AI-Generated Identity and Deepfake Onboarding

cn.rt: Synthetic and deepfake identities in remote applications drive bust-out, loan fraud and mule use; voice cloning hits phone banking.

T.n: Unhosted Wallets and Peer-to-Peer Exchange Abuse

cn.rt: Customers send fiat to exchanges and P2P sellers for unhosted wallets, often scam-driven; seen through everyday account payments.

T.n: Virtual Asset Laundering via Mixers, Tumblers and Chain-Hopping

cn.rt: Cybercrime proceeds, ATO, scams and mule cash-out on retail accounts, card fraud and loan fraud, via digital and phone social engineering.

T.n: Drug Trafficking and Precursor Chemicals (incl. Synthetic Opioids)

cn.rt: Drug cash placed as many small deposits into retail accounts then moved on digitally; lifestyle spend funded by cash.
Customers fund offshore or unlicensed betting via card and bank payments, and use accounts as pass-through wallets; mostly digital.
Retail cash proceeds of illicit tobacco deposited via everyday accounts at branch; trade and merchant elements are out of consumer scope.

T.n: Market abuse (insider dealing, wash trading, pump-and-dump) as a predicate and laundering vehicle

cn.rt: Victims pay protection or loan-shark money from personal accounts, with coerced cash withdrawals, accompanied visits and collector accounts; personal loans taken to pay.
